races.name: Meath Farm Machinery Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Alex Belardo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with visors who has won over this sort of trip before; 14 days since last run, trainer cold at 0/25 over 14 days, and her similar-going record reads 0 wins from 15 attempts — she is a pace-setter whose chief role here may be to set the race up for others.
runners_data.comment: Won a handicap at Down Royal by half a length last time when stepped back down in trip, confirming he handles this distance and going well. First-time visor today; the trainer's current figures are the main caveat.

runners_data.name: Annacroft
runners_data.note: Lightly raced, OR=120 and clearly here on talent rather than form, but a single run (9th of 13 over 13f on Soft) gives almost no read; undefined style, fades in the finish, and the McConnell yard is 1/27 over 14 days — treat with caution.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way in a maiden at Down Royal on her only outing, where she looked inexperienced and never threatened; all to prove stepping into handicap company. The wide draw at stall 14 adds to the task, though her pedigree suggests a mile could suit.

runners_data.name: Gloriously Glam
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with three wins on Good going at 6-7f and a solid course record (8 runs, 3W 4P on similar going); trainer McGuinness in form at 3/27 over 14 days and Leigh Roche is a positive booking — travels handily and finishes out the trip.
runners_data.comment: Effective at seven to eight furlongs, but well held at Limerick last time when back up in trip, and her previous win came in a claiming race — a step up in quality is needed. First-time cheekpieces today.

runners_data.name: Hexagonal
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner who will dispute early with Alex Belardo; wears a tongue-tie and a paceband, has placed once on Good ground, and 15 days since last run; the sustained early battle could leave both pace horses vulnerable in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Ridden too prominently at Leopardstown last time and beaten seven lengths; two below-par efforts now to overcome. Tongue-tie and cheekpieces applied together for the first time today, and he is effective over today's trip and ground.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: Prominent type fitted with tongue-tie and paceband, ran just two days ago which is worth flagging; has placed twice on similar going and McGuinness double-handed here — needs to recover quickly but has the positional profile to be competitive if fresh enough.
runners_data.comment: Racing again just two days after her last run; she went forward too eagerly at Fairyhouse and was beaten five lengths there. Handles this trip and going, has competed off higher marks, and adds tongue-tie and cheekpieces today, though stall 16 is wide.

runners_data.name: Smithfield
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing a hood who has a modest record on Good going (0W 1P from 6 runs on similar); trainer Cromwell is 2/32 over 14 days and recent form shows double-figure finishes — likely to be covered up off the pace but lacks the finishing kick to win.
runners_data.comment: Below par at Leopardstown last time, beaten over seven lengths without a clear reason; his record in recent starts is inconsistent. First-time blinkers could help, and he handles this distance and ground, but a more dependable showing is needed.

runners_data.name: Buttermere Ridge
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who fades in the finish; ORs a decent 68 but the form line (/600-7) is dire and similar-going record is 0W 0P from 10 runs — hard to trust even if the race sets up perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Effective over seven to ten furlongs on today's ground, with first-time tongue-tie alongside a retained visor — he was arguably too prominent at Leopardstown last time and beaten seven lengths, so the headgear change could prove the key. A declining run of form is the main reservation.

runners_data.name: Dynamic Force
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who ran just one day ago which is a significant fitness question; has placed twice on similar going and has consistent mid-pack finishes — could benefit from a strong pace but the back-to-back scheduling is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Racing for the second day running, he found the shorter trip at Fairyhouse too sharp last time and was beaten eight lengths; returning to eight furlongs suits his profile. Handles the going and is competitively placed, but needs to bounce back on a quick turnaround.

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted hold-up horse who has won on Good ground (1W 2P from 5 similar-going runs); 35 days since last run for a usually-busy McGuinness yard and Rory Cleary takes the ride — the freshness is worth noting, and the style suits a genuinely-run race.
runners_data.comment: Down in class today and ran creditably at Down Royal last time, beaten just over two lengths over a shorter trip; effective over eight to eleven furlongs and handles today's going well. First-time hood applied; a 35-day absence is his only question mark.

runners_data.name: Rampage
runners_data.note: Prominent racer fitted with a tongue-tie and visors whose form reads 086700 — consistent non-winner who finds himself out of contention in the final furlong; apprentice rider Tormey takes over for the McCourt yard which is 0/7 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Beaten seven lengths at Leopardstown last time continuing a run of poor displays; racing again here just a day later with first-time tongue-tie and visor applied. Handles this distance and going and his mark has been edged down, but considerably more is needed from him.

runners_data.name: Colugo
runners_data.note: Veteran stayer whose natural home is a staying trip (has run over 12-18f); a true hold-up horse pushed to midfield on the map because the rear is overcrowded — racing well out of his comfort zone at 1m, and the STYLE_FIT of 0.90 reflects that his chance depends on a scenario that is unlikely to materialise.
runners_data.comment: Usually races from the rear and the soft ground at Leopardstown last time may have hindered her; effective over today's trip, adding a first-time tongue-tie. Her form in both codes this season has been poor, and stall 17 is wide.

runners_data.name: Je Suis Celebre
runners_data.note: Undefined-style runner with two placed efforts on Soft/Standard going but unplaced over 8f and 10f on Good; 36 days since last run for a small Thorne yard (1/7 over 14 days) and OR=67 is competitive — could be value if the race is strongly run.
runners_data.comment: Drops in class today and his Fairyhouse run on a longer trip is best overlooked; effective at seven to eight furlongs and handles today's going. Top-rated here, adding first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces — the wide draw is the only slight concern.

runners_data.name: Lohengrin
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose record shows consistent double-figure finishes (10th, 11th, 14th, 20th) and a "fades in finish" flag; the tongue-tie and paceband haven't helped, the trainer is 0/2 over 14 days, and being displaced from his preferred rear position further reduces his chance — STYLE_FIT 0.91.
runners_data.comment: Run of poor efforts has persisted, beaten six lengths at Leopardstown last time with his form heading the wrong way; first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces added today. Handles today's distance and is better on a sound surface, but considerably more is needed to reverse this decline.

runners_data.name: Tara Na Ri
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from the Meade yard who fades late and has run twice in the last two days — barely 48 hours between runs is a striking scheduling fact; form reads 8-0050 and similar-going record is 0W 0P from 4 runs.
runners_data.comment: Racing again quickly, just two days after his last outing; found the pace too hot at Fairyhouse and was beaten over seven lengths, looking as if he needed further. Today's longer trip is a positive, but the form record leaves a lot to prove.

runners_data.name: Countertop
runners_data.note: Two-year-old with an OR of 120 that looks like a data anomaly; four runs show consistent no-shows (0, 7, 16, 16), ridden by a 7lb claimer for a yard cold at 1/19 over 14 days, and 260 days off — the long absence and age make this a very speculative entry.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a 260-day absence and has yet to show much over distances up to eight furlongs; was well beaten in a maiden at The Curragh on his most recent start. Hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Mullacash Buzz
runners_data.note: Prominent racer fitted with tongue-tie and paceband who has placed twice in this sort of company; an 8-year-old running on one day's rest (1d since last run) and the Dowling yard is 0/4 over 14 days — place claims rather than win claims.
runners_data.comment: Went off too quickly at Roscommon last time and was beaten nine lengths; adds tongue-tie and cheekpieces today. Usually races from the front and handles this trip, but appears better suited to the all-weather, and his turf form has been inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Wonderwalk
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose entire form base is over extreme distances (10-18f) on Good ground — mapped to midfield due to redistribution but clearly out of his element at 1m; STYLE_FIT 0.90 and 0W 0P from 8 similar-going starts confirms the trip is the primary concern.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way on her return to the Flat at Leopardstown last time and her form in both codes has been poor; hard to fancy against these rivals. First-time hood added today, but significant improvement is needed.

races.paceDynamic: Alex Belardo and Hexagonal are the two confirmed front-runners in a 17-runner field, and with both drawn to go forward from the outset, there will be a genuine contest for the early lead that should produce an honest, pressured gallop across the 1m trip on Good turf at Bellewstown. The field is unusually pace-laden at the front: Gloriously Glam, Minaun View, Smithfield, and Rampage will all try to press or sit prominently, meaning the early stages are likely to be busier than normal and the pace unlikely to relent. Three true hold-up horses — Colugo, Lohengrin, and Wonderwalk — have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the field is already saturated with hold-up types, meaning none of those three is likely to get their natural position; Alex Belardo and Hexagonal are far better placed to dominate proceedings than any of the pushed-back horses. A genuinely contested early pace over a flat mile on Good ground strongly favours horses with prominent or handy racing styles who can travel fluently into the contest and finish out the trip rather than late-running hold-up types who will find traffic and insufficient cover in such a compressed field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Alex Belardo and Hexagonal fight for the lead and set a genuine gallop, leaving prominent racers to travel handily through the race.
scenarios.body: If Alex Belardo and Hexagonal fight for the lead and set a genuine gallop, leaving prominent racers to travel handily through the race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace horses — most likely Alex Belardo — steals a march and is not pressed hard enough to weaken in the straight.
scenarios.body: If one of the two pace horses — most likely Alex Belardo — steals a march and is not pressed hard enough to weaken in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and burns out both front-runners, allowing a horse tracking at the rear of the prominent group to run through the field late.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is genuinely strong and burns out both front-runners, allowing a horse tracking at the rear of the prominent group to run through the field late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed runners manage to find space and the race is run at a tempo fast enough to bring genuine closers into it from the rear.
scenarios.body: If the redistributed runners manage to find space and the race is run at a tempo fast enough to bring genuine closers into it from the rear.

watchPoints.text: Alex Belardo and Hexagonal will both attempt to lead from the gates — watch the first two furlongs for a speed duel that could compromise both horses' finishing efforts and benefit any horse travelling prominently just off the pace.

Minaun View ran just 2 days ago and Dynamic Force and Rampage both ran 1 day ago — if any of these horses show signs of sluggishness in the early stages, the pace shape could thin out at the front and allow Alex Belardo to dominate unchallenged.

Land Of The Giants is 35 days off the track for the usually-active McGuinness yard; a yard with three runners in this race (Gloriously Glam, Minaun View) suggests confidence, but the absence is worth monitoring in the parade ring.

Colugo, Lohengrin, and Wonderwalk are all true hold-up or staying types who cannot get their natural position in this compressed field — if any of these are seen travelling surprisingly well through the race, it may indicate a stronger early pace than anticipated rather than form improvement.

Countertop's OR=120 in a field where most rivals are rated 40-69 looks anomalous for a two-year-old with four poor runs; watch the market for any sign of stable confidence, but the 260-day absence and juvenile profile in a claimer are both red flags.

races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series (C & G) Maiden

runners_data.name: High Morals
runners_data.comment: Failed to deliver on debut at The Curragh where he was backed to perform well, beaten five and a half lengths; a 60-day break since and he is likely capable of better. The top course jockey is a positive, though he needs to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Full Volume
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye on debut at Down Royal, travelling strongly before finishing beaten three and a half lengths in an auction race; acts on soft and handles today's distance. Should come on for the experience and has plenty in his favour.

runners_data.name: Celestial Heights
runners_data.comment: Debut today and faces a tough enough task; an Earthlight gelding whose dam showed smart form at seven furlongs and was a multiple winner on the all-weather. Pedigree suggests he could be capable, but he needs to learn on the job.

runners_data.name: Cudawudashuda
runners_data.comment: A debut colt by a high-class miler whose dam was a useful performer at a mile; his half-brother showed sharp form at six furlongs, and the yard gets its horses ready for their first start. Bred to handle today's trip and looks a notable contender, despite the trainer's lean current spell.

runners_data.name: Kraar
runners_data.comment: Close second at Down Royal last time, beaten half a length when stepped up in trip on softer ground; acts on today's conditions and is bred for a mile. Top-rated here for a leading yard and likely to progress further.

runners_data.name: Rock On Johnny
runners_data.comment: Debut today from a yard whose horses tend to need time to reach their best; a Dubawi Legend gelding whose dam was unraced, so the pedigree offers little guidance. May need this outing to learn.

runners_data.name: Supreme Act
runners_data.comment: Beaten six lengths on debut in an auction race at Down Royal, with room to improve for the experience; handles today's distance and is expected to come on. The wide draw at stall 10 is the main question.

runners_data.name: Chico Guapo
runners_data.comment: Inexperienced and never a factor in his last start at Gowran Park, down the field, and a major step forward is required to get involved today. Hard to fancy on his current level of form.

runners_data.name: Come On Noddy
runners_data.comment: Inexperienced on his only start at Navan, where he showed nothing and was well beaten; all to prove here. Speed in the pedigree is a positive, but stall 8 is wide and he must show significant improvement.

runners_data.name: Pennsylvania Ave
runners_data.comment: Debut from a yard that has landed three of the last five runnings, trained by a top course handler; his dam showed smart form at eight furlongs. Should go well on pedigree, though stall 9 is wide.

races.name: Smiths Of Drogheda Ford Classic Handicap

runners_data.name: Lahore Da King
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter who should cross to the front unchallenged; form figures of 401070 are modest but the horse is in its comfort zone on good ground and has won over this trip, and trainer Mullins has one winner from four runners in the last 14 days — the key question is whether it can resist the prominent pack when pressure arrives.|
runners_data.comment: Won at this course in April off a lower mark, and the shorter trip here is a positive after a dire last effort at a longer distance; effective on this going and distance. First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces today, though he has been inconsistent and the mark still asks questions.

runners_data.name: Zipster
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride on this consistent five-year-old who has placed twice on good ground in five similar-going starts; drawn to race prominently, 79 days off the track is a minor concern but McMonagle's booking is significant and the horse ran well over this trip and distance before.|
runners_data.comment: Third at Leopardstown on his most recent outing, four lengths off the pace; effective over today's distance on this ground and off a 79-day break. In decent form and holds solid claims.

runners_data.name: Kitty Bear
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's four-year-old won over 8f on good and has two wins from 29 trainer runners in the last 14 days — active yard in form; the horse's prominent style suits a race likely to be won from just off the pace, and good-ground form (1W, 1P from three similar starts) is encouraging.|
runners_data.comment: Won by three lengths at Roscommon off a lower mark two runs ago and handles this distance and going well; she was below her best last time over a shorter trip, which is excusable. Back on the same mark, the wide draw at stall 13 is the main negative.

runners_data.name: Bucaneer's Spirit
runners_data.note: Carries 136lbs but boasts the best similar-going profile in the field with 12 qualifying runs, two wins and four places on good ground; Gary Carroll's booking adds confidence, and the horse has run consistently well over this trip and shorter, making it one of the most reliable forecasters in this scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Won at Cork off a lower mark earlier in the season and has held his form since; ran to his level last time beaten five lengths off today's same mark. Effective over the distance and going, with that mark looking lenient on his best run.

runners_data.name: Darkdeserthighway
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the mount on this eight-year-old hold-up type who has placed three times on Flat/AW tracks in recent starts; the 112-day absence is a concern and all five recent runs came on Standard or Flat going rather than turf good, which creates a small but real uncertainty about conditions.|
runners_data.comment: Returning after a 112-day layoff with first-time blinkers; ran well at Dundalk last time, beaten one and a half lengths off a mark higher than today's. Generally consistent at this distance and handles the going, though a better surface usually suits her best.

runners_data.name: Free Solo
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner at heart but pushed back to midfield here because the field simply cannot accommodate another prominent type; Chris Hayes rides a nine-year-old who has won twice on good ground in nine similar-going runs — if it finds a lead-adjacent spot early despite the crowd, it could be dangerous, but racing against its natural style tempers expectation.|
runners_data.comment: Fifth at Leopardstown last time beaten five lengths, running to his current level; best suited to seven furlongs but handles any ground. First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces added, though his form has been moderate and a step forward is needed to get involved.

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: Six-year-old stepping back in trip from 10f, where three of five recent runs took place; Siobhan Rutledge rides for a trainer without a recent run, and the horse has no wins from seven similar-going starts, making it hard to make a case even if the race falls perfectly.|
runners_data.comment: Held up from off the pace at Roscommon last time and finished well beaten, never getting into the race; a marked revival is needed here. Handles the distance and going, but the wide draw at stall 14 does not help.

runners_data.name: Comfort Line
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has placed three times on good ground in three similar-going starts and won over this trip at Leopardstown; Adrian McGuinness is active (3/20 last 14 days) and the horse's visor is freshly applied — but being a natural prominent type forced into a midfield slot means Gabriella Hill (7) faces a tricky task getting it to its best position.|
runners_data.comment: Won by a neck off a lower mark at Dundalk two runs back and ran to form last time, second beaten three lengths despite missing the break — one pound lower today. Effective over today's distance on any going; first-time visor added on a short break.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Dreams
runners_data.note: Ben Coen on a four-year-old with one win and six places from nine good-ground starts — the best prominence profile in the field statistically; as a genuine pace-lover squeezed into midfield by the sheer volume of similar types, the trainer Ciaran Murphy has two winners from 14 runners in the last fortnight, suggesting the yard is live.|
runners_data.comment: Third at Leopardstown last time, beaten just over three lengths back up in trip, coming back to her best; on her previous winning mark and handles this distance and a sound surface. Draw 1 is a positive, and she has a chance if that form holds.

runners_data.name: Variance
runners_data.note: Three-year-old returning after 233 days off for Dr Richard Newland & Jamie Insole — an Irish debut for a yard rarely seen at Bellewstown; hold-up style on a circuit where closers need luck in running, and the lengthy absence makes confidence in a big run difficult to justify.|
runners_data.comment: Returning after 233 days off and beaten over eight lengths in a claimer at Dundalk on his most recent outing; his form over today's distance is unproven, and he may not get home over a mile. Hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Rockbury Lad
runners_data.note: Ran just yesterday (1-day turnaround) and the fades-in-finish flag is a real concern; the seven-year-old is a true hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield slot on the map, and with 10 from 15 similar-going runs finishing out of the frame, the race setup does not suit.|
runners_data.comment: Showed improved form at Leopardstown last time on quicker ground, beaten just over six lengths; a sound surface suits him and the handicapper appears to have given him a reasonable chance. First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces today, though he remains yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Glamazon
runners_data.note: Shane Foley on a three-year-old who won over 10f on good and has run well in better company; five winners from 29 trainer runners in 14 days for Mrs Harrington is a strong yard angle, and the blinkers applied could sharpen a horse that has shown the ability to quicken — a genuine danger if the race turns into a sprint from two out.|
runners_data.comment: Won at this trip in the past and handles soft and good ground, but was well beaten at Leopardstown last time, possibly struggling on testing conditions; first-time blinkers added today. A better effort is needed, and she has the ability to return to form.

runners_data.name: Imnotleavinyou
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good just two days ago — a tight turnaround but the horse is clearly in excellent form (155 form figure) and trainer Michael Mulvany has one winner from nine recent runners; the hold-up style means it needs either a strong pace or a fortunate split in the field, but recent good-ground wins over shorter trips suggest it will stay the mile well.|
runners_data.comment: Won at Limerick three runs back off a lower mark; fifth last time beaten two lengths on today's same mark, running to her level. Effective over this trip with cut in the ground, adding a first-time tongue-tie — the mark asks slightly more but she is trending positively.

runners_data.name: Smaoineamh Sile
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old who fades in finishes and whose entire recent form has come on Standard going — six from 15 similar-going runs is misleading context as most came on AW not turf good; the 171-day absence compounds the worry and this looks a difficult assignment.|
runners_data.comment: Below par in a visor at Dundalk on her most recent start and returning after 171 days off; inconsistent in form and needs to show considerably more here. Handles this distance and ground, tends to race prominently, and adds first-time tongue-tie today.

runners_data.name: Tariff
runners_data.note: Two-year-old with just four career runs all on Standard going and a fades-in-finish tendency; Nathan Crosse on a 198-day returnee who has finished 9th, 10th, 6th and 13th — the hold-up style and inexperience on turf make this a learning exercise rather than a winning proposition.|
runners_data.comment: Missed the start and wandered under pressure at Dundalk last time, beaten over seven lengths; returning after nearly 200 days off with questions over the distance. Usually held up, and hard to recommend against these opponents.

races.paceDynamic: Lahore Da King is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no serious challenger for the lead, should be allowed to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop around Bellewstown's flat mile. Behind him, the field is heavily loaded with prominent types — Free Solo, Comfort Line, Bay Of Dreams, Bucaneer's Spirit, Zipster, Kitty Bear and Glamazon all want to race handy — meaning a fierce battle for the early berths directly behind the leader will compress the race into a cavalry charge rather than a true test of stamina. The hold-up horses (Darkdeserthighway, Variance, Rockbury Lad, Imnotleavinyou, Smaoineamh Sile, Tariff) will be pushed further back than ideal by the traffic ahead, reducing their ability to deliver a clean late run. This race shape — a single unhurried leader, a bunched prominent pack grinding for position, and closers buried in traffic — most strongly favours genuinely versatile prominent horses who can secure a clean run just behind the leader and outstay rivals in a steadily-run contest, rather than pure hold-up types who will struggle to find clear daylight. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate; Free Solo, Comfort Line and Bay Of Dreams are the most likely to actually secure a forward position despite being redistributed on the map, while others will be forced to race in unnatural midfield slots.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Lahore Da King dictates an honest but unhurried gallop and the prominent pack settles just behind without fracturing the pace.
scenarios.body: If Lahore Da King dictates an honest but unhurried gallop and the prominent pack settles just behind without fracturing the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Compounds, Pack Splits
scenarios.trigger: If Lahore Da King sets too slow a tempo and the race turns into a messy sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: If Lahore Da King sets too slow a tempo and the race turns into a messy sprint from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops a true end-to-end gallop that strings the field out and creates gaps for closers to exploit.
scenarios.body: If the race develops a true end-to-end gallop that strings the field out and creates gaps for closers to exploit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Outsider Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the scrum for prominent positions causes interference and interference disrupts the fancied horses' runs.
scenarios.body: If the scrum for prominent positions causes interference and interference disrupts the fancied horses' runs.

watchPoints.text: Bucaneer's Spirit and Kitty Bear — both prominent racers with strong similar-going profiles and active trainer form; if either secures a clean run tracking Lahore Da King into the straight, they are the primary beneficiaries of the expected race shape.

The scrum for prominent positions behind Lahore Da King involves at least six horses — Free Solo, Comfort Line, Bay Of Dreams, Zipster, Glamazon and Bucaneer's Spirit — watch the first two furlongs for interference as they jostle for ground, which could compromise several fancied runners.

Imnotleavinyou ran yesterday and Rockbury Lad ran yesterday too — both are hold-up types on tight turnarounds; if either shows any signs of a quick-back bounce it could factor late, but the traffic situation from the rear makes a clear run difficult to guarantee.

Darkdeserthighway with Colin Keane is the most interesting hold-up horse if the pace quickens genuinely, but all five recent runs came on non-turf going — watch the market move to assess whether connections believe the good turf conditions are suitable.

Glamazon's blinkers application for Mrs Harrington combined with Shane Foley's booking is worth noting as a market mover; if the race turns into a sprint from two out rather than a true test, the three-year-old's turn of foot could make it a danger in Scenario B.

runners_data.name: Bold Commander
runners_data.comment: Speed in his pedigree and from a top yard, Bold Commander showed a touch of ability on debut at The Curragh despite some greenness; significant improvement is expected with that experience behind him, and he shapes as a genuine danger here.

runners_data.name: Howlin Wolf
runners_data.comment: Still seeking his first win after back-to-back seventh-place finishes, Howlin Wolf showed modest improvement second time out at Navan but remains well held; his sprint pedigree is the best angle, and more is needed to get competitive here.

runners_data.name: New Mexico
runners_data.comment: Sprint-bred colt who was found well held at The Curragh last time, pushed along hard in a competitive maiden; he returns on the back of a short break and handles today's distance, but needs to show significant improvement to threaten.

runners_data.name: Tradewinds
runners_data.comment: Consistent and well-related, Tradewinds was runner-up at Down Royal on his latest start, having also placed in one of his two prior outings; sprint-bred and effective on today's ground, he arrives with strong claims, though he remains without a win from three recent starts.

runners_data.name: Two Brigade
runners_data.comment: Sprint-bred and showing some improvement on his second outing at Naas last time, where he was beaten 9l, Two Brigade remains well held and faces a tough task to get off the mark; significantly more is needed to feature here.

runners_data.name: Alrashdeyah
runners_data.comment: Unable to build on her debut effort when upped in class last time, Alrashdeyah has an easier opportunity here and tries a first-time hood; acts at 6f on today's ground and must come back to form, but if she does she has genuine claims.

runners_data.name: April Mist
runners_data.comment: Runner-up on debut at Naas where she finished with purpose over today's trip, April Mist looks sure to progress further and partners a top course rider; acts on good ground, bred for speed, and rates a clear standout as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Little Diva
runners_data.comment: On debut from a yard that has shown an aptitude with newcomers, Little Diva should be at home over 5f; that said, her modest purchase price and lack of form mean the market is the best guide here.

races.name: Landy, Muldoon & Co Maiden

runners_data.name: Reposado
runners_data.note: Has placed twice in Good-ground 6f company and drops to 5f here, where a prominent, pressing style suits a slow-tempo race; Donagh O'Connor rides for a trainer with one win from eight in a 14-day window, and 15 days between runs is fine — form line suggests consistent participation without winning but the tactical position is ideal.
runners_data.comment: Frustrating in nature but a drop in trip today looks a definite plus for Reposado, who failed to stay the distance at Leopardstown last time; has course and distance form and handles these conditions, though getting off the mark demands a more consistent display.

runners_data.name: Banish Misfortune
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who will get a soft lead unchallenged — the fading-in-finish flag is the key concern, as a comfortable early clip may preserve enough for a brave display, though maiden form is sparse (single run, 16th on Soft over 7f) and the OR of 120 looks anomalous in this context.
runners_data.comment: Racing very keenly and taking herself to the lead at Limerick, Banish Misfortune had nothing left in the tank when the race developed and was well beaten on her only start; a mixed pedigree with a sprint sire, she looks likely to need more time.

runners_data.name: Ennoble
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's yard runs at a sharp 14-day strike rate (16/79) and Dylan Browne McMonagle is a significant booking; Ennoble holds 5f Good-ground form (placed once in five) and is a natural hold-up type who needs the tempo to be honest — 48 days off is the query.
runners_data.comment: Generally consistent as a juvenile and still a notable player on that two-year-old form, Ennoble came to grief at Navan last time; conditions and trip suit, he trains with a top course handler, and a big chance awaits if he comes here ready to run.

runners_data.name: Profit Surge
runners_data.note: Consistent placer whose best efforts come at 6-7f on Good to Soft ground, so the drop to 5f and a slow pace are mild concerns; Colin Keane's presence is notable, the tongue tie is a positive flag, and the prominent style means tactical positioning won't be an issue.
runners_data.comment: Admirably consistent, Profit Surge was a close second at Fairyhouse last time in a claimer, though that form may slightly overstate her claims here; goes in first-time blinkers, acts over 7-8f on today's ground, and with a top jockey aboard she merits serious consideration.

runners_data.name: Sparky Sparky
runners_data.note: Switches to a hood today having run a solid 2nd over 5f Good ground recently — a genuine hold-up type who needs a strong gallop to maximise closing speed; Ben Coen is a strong rider but 19 days since last run is straightforward, and the concern is the lack of a true pace injection to bring this one into the race.
runners_data.comment: Having responded well to first-time cheekpieces at Cork last time — a close second beaten just 1½l — Sparky Sparky retains them here; an in-form trainer supports his chance, and if reproducing that level from a consistent recent position, he is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Focaccia
runners_data.note: Ran 2nd over 5f on Standard ground and shows enough pace in its profile to be competitive — however, its true running style is that of a hold-up horse, pushed forward on the map only because rear positions are crowded; the 6-day turnaround is quick, and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers optimism if the pace is merely steady.
runners_data.comment: Beaten four and a half lengths at The Curragh last time from a drop in class, Focaccia has shown promise over 5f on this ground; questions about her temperament remain a factor, but she arrives in decent form and is a genuine danger if at her best here.

runners_data.name: Kidd
runners_data.note: Completely unknown quantity — unknown days since last run, unknown form, tongue tie fitted, and the going is marked UNKNOWN; a 7lb claim from Jessica Maye helps the weight, and trainer John C McConnell has a reasonable 14-day window (3/16), but this is a horse to treat as a pure wildcard.
runners_data.comment: A debut filly by a high-class sprinting sire out of a useful sprinting mare, Kidd has the bloodlines to handle this trip and should be effective at 5f; but with a modest purchase price and no form to assess, the market will tell more than the form book here.

runners_data.name: White Smoke
runners_data.note: Has an eye-catching 2nd (6f, Soft) in its recent past and the gelding switch (tb headgear) is noted — a natural hold-up horse repositioned to midfield on the map because the rear is congested, and 55 days off is the longer query; McCullagh rides and the STYLE_FIT flag means this shape may not play to its strengths.
runners_data.comment: Off a short break and stepping down from a handicap at Naas where she struggled, White Smoke tries first-time blinkers here; effective at 6f on today's conditions and with some placed form in her record, she is inconsistent and must prove more than that most recent display.

races.paceDynamic: Banish Misfortune is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f maiden at Bellewstown and, with no genuine rival willing to press for the lead, is set to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. Reposado and Profit Surge will attempt to track close to the pace from prominent positions, while Ennoble, Sparky Sparky, White Smoke, and Focaccia are all natural hold-up or rear-positioned types — though White Smoke and Focaccia have been redistributed to midfield on the map precisely because the field holds more true hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear. With Banish Misfortune uncontested and setting an honest but unhurried tempo on Good ground, the race is likely to set up as a test of sustained speed rather than a searching end-to-end gallop, which limits the raw closing kick available to the genuine hold-up runners. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel close to the controlled pace and produce their effort early in the straight, rather than horses needing a truly strong gallop to generate momentum from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Banish Misfortune sets a measured, uncontested pace and prominent runners track comfortably before asserting in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Banish Misfortune sets a measured, uncontested pace and prominent runners track comfortably before asserting in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Banish Misfortune, despite its fading-in-finish flag, finds enough in a muddling pace to simply outstay a fractured pursuit.
scenarios.body: If Banish Misfortune, despite its fading-in-finish flag, finds enough in a muddling pace to simply outstay a fractured pursuit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Cuts Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a true hold-up horse picks up the gaps in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a true hold-up horse picks up the gaps in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Bunching
scenarios.trigger: If a sluggish start or mid-race checks cause the field to bunch, opening the race to any runner regardless of style.
scenarios.body: If a sluggish start or mid-race checks cause the field to bunch, opening the race to any runner regardless of style.

watchPoints.text: Reposado and Profit Surge are the two prominent types most likely to benefit if Banish Misfortune's controlled gallop sets up a track-and-pounce finish — watch whether either gets a clear sit just off the leader's quarters from the off.

Banish Misfortune's fading-in-finish flag is critical — if it is caught inside the final furlong by prominent pursuers, the race resolves quickly, so monitor its position at the 1f pole to judge whether it is travelling or struggling.

White Smoke and Focaccia are genuine hold-up types forced into midfield positions; if the pace does not quicken sufficiently, both may find themselves neither close enough to the leader nor able to generate a late run — watch whether either can manufacture cover and a clean passage.

Kidd is a complete unknown and the lightly raced flag with no disclosed last-run date means any market move in the final minutes before post time should be treated as significant new information worth noting.

Sparky Sparky's hood is fitted for the first time (or re-fitted) — watch how the horse loads and settles in the early furlongs, as the headgear change could materially alter its position in the early stages relative to its usual hold-up pattern.

races.name: Eco Bullet Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Viamonte
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on good ground where she has form (9 runs on similar going, four placings), trained by T Browne with a 1/1 T14 strike rate; 26 days since last run looks fresh, but needs the pace to collapse to get to the front.
runners_data.comment: Needing that reappearance run at Navan and finishing well down the field there, Viamonte arrives fitter now and switches to first-time cheekpieces; handles a variety of ground conditions and has placed form earlier in the campaign, though more is needed to feature in a competitive handicap.

runners_data.name: Happy Henry
runners_data.note: The confirmed front runner here, though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) notes he is racing slightly out of his most comfortable role; McCreery has a poor 14-day record (0/15) and he was last out just 9 days ago — his ability to control this race is the pivotal pace question.
runners_data.comment: In fine fettle since landing at Navan two starts back, Happy Henry was a solid third last time off the same mark as today; tries first-time cheekpieces, handles 5-6f on a range of conditions, and connections have a strong record in this race.

runners_data.name: Bye Bye Now
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from a 93-day break for McConnell (1/14 T14), who won over 5f on Tapeta (STA) last time; the step back to good turf is a query given all five history runs are on Tapeta, making her going profile genuinely uncertain on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Steadily progressive through recent starts, Bye Bye Now landed a race earlier this season before running fourth at Dundalk last time, just 2l behind the leader off a mark 2lb higher than today's; effective at 5-6f on AW and back after a break, she has claims.

runners_data.name: Sceitimini
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse flagged as fading in the finish and absent 161 days; Colin Keane's booking is the attraction, and he has shown ability over 5f on good, but the lengthy layoff combined with a fade tendency makes him hard to trust even with the top jockey aboard.
runners_data.comment: Showing encouragement at Dundalk last time, held up patiently and beaten just 2l, Sceitimini is open to improvement with restraint applied at this trip; off for over five months but a top rider takes the mount, and he looks an interesting contender.

runners_data.name: Dandy Land
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type who also fades in the finish — carried to midfield on the map because of the volume of hold-up horses in this field; three of five runs on good ground produced finishes of 8th or worse, and the STYLE_FIT discount (0.90) underlines the positional squeeze he faces.
runners_data.comment: Effective at 6f and with a trainer who has a strong record in this contest, Dandy Land was beaten further than expected at Fairyhouse last time, failing to build on her prior form; she remains open to better in handicaps but needs a sharper showing here.

runners_data.name: Plushy
runners_data.note: Hold-up style, 3-year-old trained by Gavin Cromwell (7/53 T14 — active yard), fitted with hood; recent form figures of 6-9-9-0 on good 5f are discouraging, though the earlier third on 6f Stan could indicate stamina is an asset in a truly run race.
runners_data.comment: Struggling in a stiffer test at Navan most recently, Plushy tries a first-time hood here and is competitively placed in an open field; acts at 5-6f on a sound surface, though she must leave that disappointing display behind and show more to get involved.

runners_data.name: Army Leave
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after a full 366 days off — a significant absence for a 2-year-old now running as a 3-year-old; third on soft last time out is the best form visible, but the layoff overrides almost every other consideration and Mulvany sends a runner back after a year with little confidence-inspiring recent evidence.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a year on the sidelines and going in a first-time tongue-tie, Army Leave went to the front too freely at Tipperary last time and had nothing left when it mattered; her maiden form likely flatters, and this looks primarily a fitness run.

runners_data.name: Platino Bianco
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on good just 9 days ago (OR=50, likely to be reassessed) and clearly handles this trip and going well; true hold-up style squeezed to midfield by the field's composition, but of all the redistributed horses his STYLE_FIT (0.93) is the strongest and his recent form is the most relevant for this scenario.
runners_data.comment: Landing at Naas last time in a tight finish after a drop in trip at a stiff track, Platino Bianco goes in first-time tongue-tie and visor here; acts at 5-6f on a sound surface but can be inconsistent, and this mark remains workable.

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with consistent placed form (three seconds, one third on good ground in last five); only 2 days since last run raises a fitness question but he has run well fresh before, and his style is genuinely suited to tracking Happy Henry in a race light on early pace.
runners_data.comment: In decent form having run second beaten 2l at Fairyhouse last time off this identical mark, Whatswrongnow comes back here just two days later; yet to get off the mark overall but handles these conditions well at 5-6f, and he is a strong contender if the quick turnaround is no issue.

runners_data.name: Steel Magnolia
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up mare with four placings from six on good/soft for McCreery — same trainer as Happy Henry; Declan McDonogh is a significant jockey booking that elevates her claims, and the visor suggests connections are trying to sharpen her up, though her true style means she needs more pace than this race is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Placed consistently in recent starts, including a close fourth at Naas last time, Steel Magnolia adds a first-time visor here; suits some cut in the ground, the trainer has a strong record in this contest, and she arrives in form as the clear one to beat.

runners_data.name: Realtin Fantasy
runners_data.note: Veteran 10-year-old hold-up horse, 245 days off, shifted to midfield on the map from a natural rear-of-field position; has shown ability over 5f on good ground (two places in last five on similar), but age, absence, and a STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) all conspire against a winning performance.
runners_data.comment: Out of form in her three most recent starts and returning from over eight months away, Realtin Fantasy tries first-time cheekpieces with an unfavourable draw also to contend with; suited by 5f on a sound surface, but plenty to prove before she can be supported with confidence.

runners_data.name: Apache Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up 7-year-old whose last five runs show four finishes of 9th or worse; the STYLE_FIT discount (0.92) and a form string of -60990 make him very hard to support regardless of the race shape, and his positional compression only adds to the challenge.
runners_data.comment: Form has tailed off in his recent starts, and Apache Star went too hard early at Naas last time, failing to sustain the effort; he tries first-time blinkers and tongue-tie here and is effective at 5f, but a significant reversal of form is required.

runners_data.name: Bel Espoir
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a fade tendency whose form figures (18th, 11th, 10th, 9th) speak for themselves — no winning form in recent history, a STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) is the lowest in the redistributed group, and a return from 9 days ago adds nothing compelling to his case.
runners_data.comment: Without a placed effort in her recent starts, Bel Espoir could not make any impression at Naas last time and lacks the form to threaten here; rated at 6f, a step up in trip may eventually help, but a significant improvement is needed first.

runners_data.name: You Smiled
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3-year-old for Andrew Slattery (4/36 T14), fitted with tongue-tie and flagged as fading in the finish; only three career runs (7th, 10th, 9th) suggest she has yet to find her form, and a STYLE_FIT score of 0.90 confirms this race shape is particularly unfavourable for her.
runners_data.comment: Carrying what looks a very lenient opening mark and going in a first-time tongue-tie, You Smiled showed more on her final maiden run at Cork last time; bred for this trip and with connections who have landed this race before, she has genuine claims here.

races.paceDynamic: Happy Henry is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead on early pace, should be able to bowl along uncontested at a sustainable gallop over this flat 5f at Bellewstown on good ground. That uncontested lead on a flat track with a steady tempo creates a rail-hugging, energy-conserving advantage that typically rewards the horse in front or those tracking closely just off the pace. Prominent racers who can latch onto Happy Henry's coattails without burning petrol — such as Bye Bye Now and Whatswrongnow — are therefore best positioned tactically. The race shape firmly favours hold-up horses capable of landing a telling late blow only if the pace is genuinely strong, which is unlikely here; prominent and front-running profiles are most advantaged. Several runners including Dandy Land, Platino Bianco, You Smiled, Steel Magnolia, Realtin Fantasy, Apache Star and Bel Espoir are true hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map because the field holds significantly more off-the-pace horses than can all settle at the rear — of these, Platino Bianco (recent winner, 5f Good specialist) is best-placed to actually deliver from that berth, but their collective style mismatch in this shape is a meaningful discount.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Happy Henry Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Happy Henry is allowed to stride into a clear, uncontested lead and controls the tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: If Happy Henry is allowed to stride into a clear, uncontested lead and controls the tempo throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Bye Bye Now or Whatswrongnow press Happy Henry harder than expected, lifting the tempo and turning it into a genuine front-runners' duel.
scenarios.body: If Bye Bye Now or Whatswrongnow press Happy Henry harder than expected, lifting the tempo and turning it into a genuine front-runners' duel.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Lands Late Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the front runners tie each other up, allowing a genuine closer to arrive with a late run.
scenarios.body: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the front runners tie each other up, allowing a genuine closer to arrive with a late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Chaos Decides
scenarios.trigger: If the large 14-runner field causes interference early and positional patterns break down entirely.
scenarios.body: If the large 14-runner field causes interference early and positional patterns break down entirely.

watchPoints.text: Happy Henry's early pace — if he is allowed to stride clear without any pressure from Bye Bye Now or Whatswrongnow, the race is almost certainly his or a prominent tracker's; any sign of a contested lead fundamentally changes the shape.

Platino Bianco at the draw/early positioning — as the most recently successful hold-up type (won 9 days ago over C&D conditions) he is the chief threat from off the pace, but Robert Whearty must thread through a 14-runner field in a 5f sprint to land a blow.

Bye Bye Now's surface switch — all five historical runs are on Tapeta (STA) and she has never run on turf; connections are confident enough to run her 93 days off but the good turf unknown is the single biggest form uncertainty in the field.

Army Leave returns from 366 days off — a 12-month absence in a 14-runner handicap deserves monitoring in the market; any significant market support would be newsworthy given no public evidence of fitness.

McCreery runs three horses (Happy Henry, Dandy Land, Steel Magnolia) with a 0/15 T14 record — the yard's recent form is poor and punters should factor in whether yard form may explain why multiple runners are needed to find a winner.

races.name: Dore & Co. Solicitors Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Rising Sky
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner at OR 60 — highest-rated horse in the field, won over 10f on Standard and has Good-ground form; at 9 days since last run and wearing a tongue-tie, she sets the shape for this entire race and is fully at home in the role she will play.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with credit at Naas nine days ago, beaten a length off this mark, and she handles today's going well, with her stamina for the trip still to prove. First-time tongue-tie and blinkers introduce a question mark, but she looks a genuine threat if she carries that effort forward.

runners_data.name: Porsche Lad
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer with a string of placed efforts on Standard trips, stepping back onto turf; trainer P J F Murphy has a poor recent strike rate (0/10 in 14 days) but the horse's natural cruising position just off the pace suits this shape well.
runners_data.comment: Has shown reliable AW form in recent starts and brings a solid speed figure, but his latest turf outing at Leopardstown left much to be desired. First-time cheekpieces could make a difference, yet proving his worth on grass remains the challenge.

runners_data.name: Cala Gracioneta
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who placed over 2m on Good last time, which is her most relevant form here; the fade flag is a concern over a strongly-run 1m4f and her trainer has had no recent winners from nine runners.
runners_data.comment: Ran second at Listowel a month ago, beaten 3 lengths off a slightly lower mark, and she handles today's trip and ground. First-time hood added, but her patchy record makes her hard to rely on repeating that improvement.

runners_data.name: Robot Rock
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who tends to fade in the closing stages; has Good-ground form over 10-12f but modest recent finishes (8th, 10th, 12th) suggest she needs a stronger pace than Rising Sky is likely to set.
runners_data.comment: Ex-French gelding who found a drop in trip counterproductive last time at Limerick, beaten 8 lengths, but the return to 12f looks far more in his favour. First-time tongue-tie added, though he still has plenty to prove for his current yard and his best form has come on AW.

runners_data.name: Jazz Forever
runners_data.note: Older hold-up type who has run over extended trips up to 17f; the fade warning is relevant over this shorter 1m4f and, while she has some Good-going credit, finishing positions have been poor in competitive company lately.
runners_data.comment: Third in his latest Flat start at Navan, beaten half a length off a mark 2lb lower than today's, which is an encouraging effort over a slightly shorter trip. Handles today's distance and going, though his record makes him unreliable to follow up.

runners_data.name: Trishuli River
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 12f on Standard and placed over similar trips; returning after 49 days but Bellewstown's turning track suits those who can press the pace, and this is a live profile if she settles well behind Rising Sky.
runners_data.comment: Reliable on the all-weather with some encouraging recent efforts, including a win in her last five starts, but her return to turf at Leopardstown was a well-beaten effort, 7½ lengths behind. First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces applied, though grass remains her primary question mark.

runners_data.name: Eastern Wind
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has won twice and placed three times in his last 15 similar-going runs — the strongest recent form record in the field; pushed into a midfield slot on the map because the field is rear-heavy, but his true role is to stalk from the back and he carries the most credible hold-up claim if the pace does open up late.
runners_data.comment: Generally a consistent performer at this level, effective over today's trip, and she rates highly on our figures at rank 3. Her last outing at Navan was well beaten without ever threatening, and the first-time cheekpieces will need to spark an improvement.

runners_data.name: Magna Gee Gee
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with modest form figures (7th, unplaced, 8th, 10th, 7th) in recent starts; has Good-ground experience but nothing in the form suggests she can make a meaningful late impact in a 19-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Held to his current level when beaten 3 lengths off this mark at Fairyhouse recently, and he handles good ground well. Effective over 10-11f but stamina over today's 12f is unproven, and his form has been in decline.

runners_data.name: Circus Act
runners_data.note: Veteran who has won over 20f — a true stayer shaped as a hold-up runner; the map places him in midfield but his natural position is further back, and at 61 days since last run (50 days for this jockey booking) the prep is not ideal.
runners_data.comment: Has the ability for this grade on her day but having done too much early over hurdles at Clonmel last time, she returns to the Flat on ground she handles. An inconsistent performer, though the conditions and trip are not beyond her.

runners_data.name: Without Love
runners_data.note: Holds wins and places on Standard ground but has no Going form figures that inspire confidence on Good turf; at 112 days off the track, fitness is a clear unknown, and while he holds up naturally his redistribution means he cannot race where he would ideally want to be.
runners_data.comment: Showed smart AW form prior to a well-beaten run at Dundalk in first-time blinkers 112 days ago. Back after a lengthy break and unexposed at this level, he could find turf more to his liking and rates as a clear danger.

runners_data.name: Sir Trancealot
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from the powerful J P Murtagh yard (2 wins from 24 in 14 days); hold-up in style with a placed run on Good ground over 12f — his lightly raced profile and trainer's current form make him one of the more interesting hold-up contenders despite the congested midfield.
runners_data.comment: Third on his handicap debut three weeks ago, beaten 2 lengths off a mark just 1lb lower, and he handles today's trip and going. Retains the cheekpieces and could benefit from a more patient approach; with the trainer in form, he warrants serious respect.

runners_data.name: Masego
runners_data.note: Won over 13f on Good ground and placed over longer trips — genuine stamina credentials; his redistribution pushes him forward on the map but he will want to hunt from the back, and the Good ground is his optimal conditions.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap 49 days ago by 2¼ lengths off a 6lb lower mark, making good use of a forward position, and he handles middle distances on soft ground. Still progressing and lightly raced, though today's mark is considerably higher.

runners_data.name: Amethyst Stone
runners_data.note: Three-year-old trained by the in-form G M Lyons (9 from 20 in 14 days) but has finished 6th, 9th, 12th and 15th in all four career starts, all on Good ground — the trainer angle is the only positive note in an otherwise uninspiring form profile.
runners_data.comment: Made a poor handicap debut at Limerick three weeks ago and the form pattern in recent starts has been inconsistent. His trainer is operating in good form of late, but conditions have yet to click for this gelding and he remains a work in progress.

runners_data.name: Sarmiento Power
runners_data.note: Consistent tail-ender on Good ground (14th, 14th, 10th in recent turf runs) with a fade flag; trainer Matthew Smith has a runner in Cala Gracioneta to focus on, and nothing in this horse's profile suggests she can threaten from her redistributed midfield berth.
runners_data.comment: Missed the break and failed to land a blow at Leopardstown recently, his latest in a run of poor form on turf, and all his better efforts have come on AW surfaces. Operates off a modest mark on today's trip but switching back to grass demands a big improvement.

runners_data.name: Idomything
runners_data.note: Low-rated hold-up type from a small stable; recent finishes of 8th, 13th, 7th, 8th and 8th paint a consistent picture of moderate ability, and being bumped forward on the map does not help a horse who needs to race from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Missed the start and finished in arrears at Down Royal 13 days ago, beaten 9½ lengths, and the overall profile in recent starts makes her hard to recommend even from a low mark. Handles today's distance and going, but improvement is needed.

runners_data.name: No Bother Aoife
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has been racing on sprint trips (7-8f) and now faces 1m4f — a sharp stamina query; the fade flag compounds the distance concern, and the redistribution means she cannot settle as far back as her natural style demands.
runners_data.comment: Effective over shorter trips and has already tired late when tried up in distance at Fairyhouse last time, making today's 12f a further stamina test. First-time tongue-tie applied; connections have a strong record in this race but she faces a stiff challenge.

runners_data.name: Private Larry
runners_data.note: Three-year-old whose form reads 8-8-13-20-10, with all Good-going starts ending in single-figure finishes near the rear; the fade tag and redistribution to midfield are both unhelpful, and the trip is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Completely failed to break at Leopardstown 15 days ago, hopelessly behind throughout and beaten 6¼ lengths. Bred for 8-10f, so today's trip is an unknown; first-time hood added, and a better run is expected at some point, though the profile makes him hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Maker's Mark
runners_data.note: Another McCourt runner (alongside Eastern Wind) from a yard with modest recent numbers; has no winning form and has finished 5th at best, with all Good-going runs producing placings of 9th, 14th and 9th — the map position does not reflect his natural hold-up tendency.
runners_data.comment: Raced far too freely and faded at Down Royal 13 days ago on a longer trip; she's best at 7-8f and today's 12f looks beyond her. Inconsistent overall, and while connections have taken this race before, she faces a considerable ask.

runners_data.name: Plus Or Minus
runners_data.note: Consistent soft-ground performer who now faces Good going for the first time in recent starts — a going concern that undermines any claims despite showing up over 12-13f; the fade flag adds further caution.
runners_data.comment: Failed to land a blow at Down Royal 13 days ago, missing the break and finishing well beaten, and his recent record in handicaps makes for difficult reading. Handles today's trip and going, but first-time tongue-tie aside, he faces a stiff task.

races.paceDynamic: Rising Sky is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 19-runner field and, with no genuine challenger disputing the lead, is set to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 1m4f trip on Good ground at Bellewstown. Porsche Lad and Trishuli River are the most likely prominent companions, tracking just off the leader and helping to set an honest but not scorching pace. Eastern Wind, Private Larry, No Bother Aoife, and several other hold-up types have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds far more closers and hold-up horses than can realistically race at the rear — Eastern Wind and Masego are the most likely to actually settle furthest back given their genuine hold-up profiles. A single, uncontested front-runner over a stamina trip on Good ground creating a controlled tempo is a shape that classically suits prominent racers and those who can travel into the race from just off the pace rather than deep hold-up specialists who will be hunting a strong late gallop that may not materialise.

watchPoints.text: Rising Sky's early stride — if she quickens away from the gate and no prominent rival matches her, she could steal a march on the large field and make this race near-impossible to reel in from midfield.

Eastern Wind's passage from the rear — with 19 runners on a turning track, the genuine hold-up types will need a clean run from 3f out; any traffic trouble turning for home effectively ends their chance in a race not run strongly enough to open gaps.

No Bother Aoife and Private Larry are stepping up significantly in trip having raced over 7-10f; if either fades sharply from the 1m mark they could cause interference for horses trying to make ground from midfield.
Amethyst Stone's trainer G M Lyons is in a rich vein of form (9/20 in 14 days) — monitor market moves, as stable support in a handicap can sometimes override a modest form profile.

With 19 runners on a tight, undulating circuit like Bellewstown, draw and early position will be critical — horses forced extremely wide on the home turn will concede significant ground regardless of finishing speed.
